BiblicalUsage: Avon is perversity — iniquity with its guilt and its punishment carried together. Cain says his punishment is greater than he can bear, God proclaims himself forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, Aaron lays the iniquities of Israel on the scapegoat, and Isaiah says the chastisement of our peace was upon him and he was wounded for our transgressions. The word holds the deed and its weight at once.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this is the word that makes the cross necessary and the cross sufficient. My iniquity was laid on him, and because he bore it, I do not have to carry its weight forever.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
